businessRules.rule: A teacher enters marks for their own subject only. A mark entered by somebody who did not mark the paper is not evidence of anything.
Every score is validated against the paper's total marks, which was fixed when the exam was created and cannot be moved afterwards.
Every student entered for the paper carries either a score or the Absent state. A blank is not a mark.
Grace marks may be awarded only where a student falls short of the passing mark by no more than the grace limit set at exam creation. A student who missed by twice the limit is not brought up.
Grace lifts a student only as far as the passing mark, never beyond it. Grace exists to turn a near miss into a pass, not to improve a grade.
Grace is refused for a student already at or above the passing mark, and more than the configured maximum is refused.

A pass achieved on grace is recorded as such, and the student's result shows that the pass was by grace and how many marks were given. A pass that reads identically to an earned one hides something the school decided.
An absent student's marks field is closed. Absent is a state on the mark, not a score of zero, and no grace may be awarded to them.
The teacher submits by the deadline set for that subject when the exam was created. After submission the teacher cannot change a mark themselves.
The Coordinator may change any submitted mark before the lock. Every change is recorded against the Coordinator's name with the previous value and a reason.
The School Admin locks the marks once they are final. After the lock no change is possible without the exam being reopened, which is a separate and deliberate act.
An absent student counts as entered for the completeness check, so the subject is not held open waiting for a mark that will never come.
Entering marks produces no grade. Grading is calculated from these marks separately, and the two locks in this module do different things.

alternateFlows.condition: A student was absent from the paper
alternateFlows.behaviour: Their marks field is closed and no score can be entered. Absent is a state on the mark, not a score of zero (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A student scored 37 against a pass mark of 40 with a grace limit of 3
alternateFlows.behaviour: Three grace marks bring them to exactly the pass mark and no further, and the pass is recorded as achieved by grace (BR-4, BR-5, BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: A student scored 35 against a pass mark of 40 with a grace limit of 3
alternateFlows.behaviour: Grace is refused, since the shortfall exceeds the limit. A student who missed by more than the limit is not brought up (BR-4).

alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Examination → Marks completeness → Enter on behalf
alternateFlows.behaviour: The Coordinator enters the marks on the teacher's behalf, and the record shows who actually entered them.
The Coordinator changes it with a reason. The teacher cannot change it themselves after submission (BR-9, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A locked mark is found to be wrong
alternateFlows.behaviour: The exam is reopened, which is a separate and deliberate act, and the correction is made before it is locked again (BR-11).

departures.requirement: A class of 40 is enterable on one screen without paging, since marking is done in a single sitting.
The grace limit, the pass-mark cap and the absent exclusion are enforced server-side. There is no route by which more grace can be awarded than the exam permits.
After the lock no route changes a mark except an explicit reopen, which is itself recorded.
Every change after submission retains its previous value, the person and the reason.
Marks and their change history are retained 7 years, matching the results calculated from them.

openQuestions.question: Who may reopen locked marks, and does it need approval above the School Admin?
openQuestions.assumption: School Admin as modelled. Not confirmed, and reopening changes a published result.

openQuestions.question: Should a pass by grace be visible to the family, or only internally?
openQuestions.assumption: Visible on the result as modelled. Confirm the school agrees.

openQuestions.question: May the Coordinator award grace, or only the subject teacher?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The Coordinator can correct a mark, which is not the same thing.

openQuestions.question: Is there a limit on how many students in a class may be passed by grace?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the report shows the count.

openQuestions.question: What happens to marks already entered if the exam is reopened and a subject rule is found wrong?
openQuestions.assumption: The rules cannot change after creation, so this cannot arise. Confirm that holds.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
